annotations.text:
Same pages, same order, same minimalism — a coherent shell around them.

What's new:
• A real app bar: grouped nav (Watch / Manage), active-page marker, and the verdict pip carried on EVERY page.
• Page bands: a title plus one sentence saying what the page is for.
• Section rules instead of a run of h3/h4.
• Tabular mono for every number.
• Cards on surfaces, hairlines everywhere else.

The one real departure: the verdict banner is now a tinted card with an accent edge rather than a full-bleed colour slab. Compare the two dashboards — if you want the slab back it's a one-line change.

Dark mode is chosen, not flipped.

The chrome takes Pico's own dark tokens. The incident ramp could not just be inverted: your grey ramp ends at #2b2b2b, which is invisible on a #13161f page.

So in dark the grey ramp runs dark → near-white instead of pale → black. 'Deeper = worse' still holds, it just runs toward light. The warm ramp keeps its direction, so warm-vs-grey separation survives at every tier.

History is shown in dark on purpose: the punchcard and the ribbon board are where that decision either works or doesn't.

Phone: 390px, the full scrolling page (not a viewport crop).

• Nav collapses to the drawer; the verdict pip stays in the bar, because knowing the verdict is why the page is open.
• Tree rows grow to 44px and drop the address — it lives on Targets.
• The glitch table restacks as cards; tables don't survive 390px.
• Theme choice (Light / Dark / System) lives in the drawer footer with the build stamp.

One thing to decide: I surfaced each target's IP next to its name on the desktop tree, where today it's only a tooltip. Easy to drop if it's noise.

This isn't five icons — it's 3 majors × an optional minor badge.

So it's designed as base + modifier. The base is one of four metaphors (A–D across the top). The modifier is identical in all four, and it isn't invented: encoding.ts already says dot = one site, bar = shared path, warm = out there. The badge is just those marks, tucked into the glyph's corner on a plate in the page colour.

Two hard rules, both testable on each board:

1. The three majors differ in SHAPE, not only hue — see the greyscale row. Colour-only would fail CVD readers and the monochrome tray.

2. Down is one shared convention everywhere: the glyph dimmed under a bold slash. It's the only treatment that still reads at 16px.

The same glyph set can drive the banner, the nav pip, a state-reflecting favicon, and the ConTray dot — which today is just a coloured blob.

Where I'd land, and why — but this is your call.

B · Path is the one that means something. It's the only direction that says 'you → your gear → the world', which is the entire thesis of the product, and it's already the Targets pipeline metaphor. It's also the tightest at 16px.

A · Signal is the safe pick: it IS your brand mark, so the favicon stays recognisably ConnectionWatcher. But rings read as Wi-Fi signal, which points at the wrong culprit, and 'struggling' thins out badly at tab size.

C · Globe fails its own greyscale row — up and struggling differ only by a dashed equator. I'd drop it.

D · Weather is the most legible of the four and the most fun, and I'd still not ship it: it spends the word 'weather' on the major axis when your product already uses it for the minor one.

If you want the meaning, take B and let me thicken it for small sizes. If you want the safety, take A.
